I'll work through each draft chapter carefully, applying the five tests and the gate test to every sentence with a potential issue.

**Ch 025 draft:**

The compression is clean. The secretary is elided but his role is covered by "the telephone purred; the secretary announced." Julius's pistol is called "Little Willie" and "the automatic" consistently. George the chauffeur is referenced but is an authorized minor-character removal — "the man at the wheel" substitutes without confusion. The anecdote-montage compression ("men he had 'shot' in Arizona, 'Frisco, the Rockies") parses. No structural damage found.

**Ch 026 draft:**

Working through carefully:

1. **"My cousin didn't think so. He didn't want us to do this."** — Jane says this. In the source, Tuppence has just said something "queer" in tone, and Jane asks about it; Jane's line responds to Tuppence's evasion about "something" on her mind. In the draft, the exchange is truncated: Tuppence says "I was thinking of something. But I don't want to tell you—not now." Then Jane says "My cousin didn't think so." The pronoun "so" dangles — "so" refers to Tommy's assurance that they'd be safe, which was Tuppence's earlier statement ("Tommy wouldn't have told us…he was sure"). But in the draft the transition drops the intermediate beat where Jane presses Tuppence. The "so" still refers back to Tommy's safety assurance from two lines earlier and a competent reader can trace it. This is merely less ornamented. Not a finding.

2. **"Then Mr. Beresford rang me—what I had already suspected—the photograph of Miss Jane Finn had never really been out of Mr. Hersheimmer's possession——"** — In the source Sir James says: "Mr. Beresford rang me up and told me, what I had already suspected, that the photograph of Miss Jane Finn had never really been out of Mr. Hersheimmer's possession." The draft renders this as: "Then Mr. Beresford rang me—what I had already suspected—the photograph of Miss Jane Finn had never really been out of Mr. Hersheimmer's possession——" The main verb of the clause ("told me") has been cut, leaving a broken syntactic structure. The sentence has no verb governing the noun clause "the photograph…had never really been out of…possession." The dash replaces "and told me, what I had already suspected, that" — but "told me" is the matrix verb. Without it the sentence reads as: "Mr. Beresford rang me — [parenthetical] — [bare noun phrase]." A competent reader cannot parse what syntactic role "the photograph…possession" plays. This is non-parseable.
